name: Starker
label: RRR Music Group
lede: A Williamsburg kid with a raspy voice, a Polo collection the company's own offices can't match, and a cartoon dog on a Westside Gunn cover. Pitchfork gave his 2026 tape an 8.4.

eras.title: Two dudes from audio school
eras.text: Starker and YL meet in an engineering class, bond over Rawkus compilations and Max B freestyles, and put out a tape that finds its first audience overseas.

years.h: Starker meets YL at the Institute of Audio Research
years.p: A mutual classmate connects them in audio engineering school. They find out they own the same records in their heads.
years.xp:
YL told The FADER he had never met anyone "this much into the same shit I was", and that Starker kept putting him on, too. Their shared canon was underground New York rap: the Rawkus Soundbombing compilations and [[Max B|372119b0-2350-455f-acd8-6371bc947531]] freestyles.

YL had already started RRR Music Group (Real Recognize Real) in 2010, according to the same FADER piece. Bandcamp Daily tells the crew's origin a little differently: it began as high-school "homie shit", with a member called MID as the first to rap and YL as the videographer. Starker was inducted in 2015.

eras.title: Lo.Ceasar
eras.text: The duo's first project. A decade later people still point to it as where the whole thing starts.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · The Harvard Crimson · Orbit
years.p: Starker's gruff, aggressive voice against YL's laid-back one. The cover put YL in the North Face Nuptse jacket that became his look.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily quotes YL on the pairing: Starker's gruff timbre is the counterpoint to his own lackadaisical flow. The project is the earliest one The Harvard Crimson credits Starker with releasing, and the Substack profile Orbit dates his public rise to it and its single "Lo Ceasar".

Its reach went past Brooklyn: YL credited the tape's impact in Japan for making a later trip possible.

eras.title: Treated like an artist
eras.text: Japan turns out to be the first place that books Starker as a performer. The duo keep returning, and the tape gets a Japanese CD.

q: I went to Japan and got treated like an artist for the first time in my life.
years.h: Starker's first solo show is in Morioka, Japan
years.p: He had been making music for nearly a decade. The mother of his child bought him the plane ticket as a Valentine's Day gift.
years.xp: The Harvard Crimson describes the 2017 trip as a turning point: after nearly ten years of making music, it was the first time he performed a solo set and it restored his confidence and his output.

years.h: Japan again: Made in Japan and a Lo.Ceasar CD
years.p: YL, Starker and RRR member MID fly to Japan and record Made in Japan there. Starker's connections there made it happen.
years.xp: YL told Bandcamp Daily that the trip was possible because of Starker's earlier connections and the response to Lo.Ceasar. A Japanese CD pressing, Lo.Ceasar Special Edition, came out in 2018 on RRR Music Group as catalog number SC-0001, with 19 tracks and beats by Wun Two, Central Parks and others, per Discogs.

years.h: Knuckleheads EP, a duo pitched like Miles and Richardson
years.p: The Modern Life magazine covers the EP in October. It frames the pair as the rap version of Darius Miles and Quentin Richardson on the Clippers.

eras.title: Polo, a cartoon dog, and a label as a uniform
eras.text: Brands notice a rapper who knows their archives better than they do. Meanwhile the music gets more tapes, more art and a first full RRR album.

years.src: Highsnobiety · The Harvard Crimson · Fresh NewSnow
years.h: Aimé Leon Dore puts Starker in a New Balance campaign
years.p: Highsnobiety later picks him as the American face of Polo Ralph Lauren's Superfan series, as a vintage Polo collector.
years.xp:
Highsnobiety's July 2022 Superfans piece shows off his apartment: a 1993 Climb rugby shirt, pieces from Polo's 1992 Stadium and 1993 Snow Beach lines, windbreakers and caps. The Crimson reports his collection includes items even Polo's corporate offices lack.

His line in that piece: "Polo will always be timeless because Polo's a part of inner-city New York culture." On July 10, 2021, RRR (Starker, YL, Zoomo) played Lot 45 in Brooklyn, and Starker told Fresh NewSnow the first second of the set felt "really locked in".

years.p: The Bandcamp page for Lo.Ceasar's return says only "WE BACK." Closer "EPCOT" is a bonus track.

years.h: Starker draws the cover for Westside Gunn's Peace "Fly" God
years.p: The Crimson says his cartoon dog, modeled on Betty Boop's Bimbo, is his signature. He had done the same for al.divino's Secrets in 2020.

years.h: RRR: The Album: 14 tracks, one label as a uniform
years.p: YL, Starker and producer Zoomo, with a tracklist that includes "Gilbert Arenas" and "Allergic to Broke".

eras.title: North Face Nace
eras.text: A double act's 2024 album gets a listening party at Aimé Leon Dore, and two years later Starker's own tape lands a Pitchfork 8.4.

years.src: Album of the Year · The FADER
years.h: Diamond Collection, named for game-worn MLB gear
years.p: YL & Starker's 17-track album takes its title from vintage baseball apparel they collect. Producers include Zoomo, Noface, Subjxct 5 and Lord Unknown.
years.xp:
The FADER reports it took a year of regular studio sessions and was one of their few records with producers beyond the in-house pair, Zoomo and Noface. The release party was held at Aimé Leon Dore's private sound room, with co-signs from Eyedress and [[Westside Gunn|9f42ba3d-3cfc-499c-ba16-7226f56b622f]].

Starker on why the record matters to him: "Every block, every business, just opens and closes so fast."

years.cap: Cover, LIVING TYPE DANGEROUS Vol. 1 "North Face Nace" (RRR Music Group, 2026)
years.src: Album of the Year · Bandcamp: Starker
years.p: Pitchfork's Alphonse Pierre gives it an 8.4. Nicholas Craven produces the most tracks, with YL and Goya Gumbani among the guests.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's summary of the tape as "Retro but never dusty", a "brilliantly bugged-out" record that sounds like "a New York that hardly exists anymore." Producers include Craven, Laron, Benji Socrate$, Lord Unknown and Foule Monk. Closer "Ronda" is a bonus track.

Starker's own Bandcamp caption calls it "BIG BROOKLYN BIG LTD SHIT!" The title plays on his own name and the North Face jackets that run through the RRR look.

yt: Starker - Banned From JPN (Prod. Nicholas Craven)
years.h: "Banned From JPN" and "Van Sons" get videos, both Craven beats
years.p: Insomniac lists "Banned From JPN", "Questlove", "Van Sons" and "Civil War" as highlights of the tape.

sources.title: Album of the Year: Starker, LIVING TYPE DANGEROUS Vol. 1
